grh_f220040d0341717766a9.title: Earth Abides Part 2
paragraphs: Years after a plague destroys civilization, Ish and Em try to turn the survivors from scavenging toward farming, but a typhoid outbreak kills much of their small community, including their first child. The survivors abandon San Francisco and begin again on fertile land, raising a new generation as old technology fails and practical skills replace it. When violent newcomer Charlie kills one of the group, the community forms a council and executes him, marking the birth of a new government. By year 48, the aged Ish has become a living legend; he passes his symbolic hammer and leadership to Joey and dies after seeing the ruined Golden Gate once more, affirming that people pass but the earth endures.

This [[show|escape|Escape]] broadcast aired on November 12, 1950. It is listed as episode 132 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Peggy Webber, Paul Frees, Lou Krugman, Jeffrey Silver, and [[person|john-dehner|John Dehner]]. Other credited names include Norman Macdonnell as director, Norman Macdonnell as producer, George R. Stewart as writer, David Ellis as radio adaptor, and Roy Rowan as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.

grh_f223592ff6064293d0f5.title: Spring Dance
paragraphs: Seventeen-year-old Bunn Williams, captain of the high-school basketball team, feels badly out of his depth at Sally Sans's sophisticated birthday dance. Convinced that wealthier Ken Carson and expensive gifts make his own dinner jacket, flowers and old-fashioned present look foolish, Bunn nearly gives up before telling Sally how he feels. Sally makes clear that the things he thought were embarrassments matter because they came from him, wears his flowers and agrees to be his girl. Their spring evening ends with Bunn wishing on the first star and Dr. Christian observing that his wish seems to have come true.
